label: low-branching
definition: A branched quality inhering in a stem or whole plant by virtue of its first branches arising low on the main axis, so that the clear trunk below the crown is short. NOTE: Common in the forestry descriptions of tropical African floras ('fût bas-branchu').
reason: A standard habit character of trees, with no term in PATO or FLOPO. 'Branched' alone loses where the branching starts.

label: medifixed
definition: An attachment quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being attached at or near its middle, so that it extends to both sides of the point of attachment. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991134 dorsifixed and FLOPO:0991135 basifixed; medifixed hairs are the T-shaped (malpighiaceous) hairs. Not FLOPO:0991136 versatile, which adds free swinging of an anther, nor FLOPO:0991107 peltate, which needs a stalk.
reason: A real attachment quality for bracts and hairs that is not covered by the FLOPO attachment classes already in place.

'Ni en creux', 'non enfoncées' = not sunk below the surrounding surface; the negation of PATO sunken.

label: obpyriform
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being pear-shaped with the broad end towards the apex, tapering towards the base or point of attachment. NOTE: Inverse of PATO:0005002 pear shaped (tapering near the top, bulging towards the base), as FLOPO:0991025 obovoid is the inverse of ovoid.
reason: A standard botanical shape for anthers and fruits. PATO has only pear shaped, which points the other way.
